# `octo/notifications`

Add `octo/notifications` to the `Octo-Capabilities` header to receive these fields.

## Contents

- [Endpoints](#endpoints)
- [Schemas introduced by this capability](#schemas-introduced-by-this-capability)
- [Source](#source)
- [Integration notes](#integration-notes)

## Endpoints

This capability unlocks 5 endpoint(s).

- **`GET /notifications/subscriptions`**: List Subscriptions.
- **`POST /notifications/subscriptions`**: Create Subscription. Body `NotificationSubscriptionRequest`.
- **`DELETE /notifications/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`**: Delete Subscription.
  - **subscriptionId** (string, in path, required): Subscription identifier.
- **`GET /notifications/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`**: Get Subscription.
  - **subscriptionId** (string, in path, required): Subscription identifier.
- **`PATCH /notifications/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`**: Update Subscription. Body `NotificationSubscriptionRequest`.
  - **subscriptionId** (string, in path, required): Subscription identifier.

## Schemas introduced by this capability

3 schema(s) exist only when `octo/notifications` is active.

### `NotificationSubscription`

Required: `subscriptionId`, `url`.

- **subscriptionId** (string, required): Subscription identifier. Example: `"sub_booking_update_01"`.
- **notificationTypes** (string[], optional): List of notification type values. Example: `["STANDARD"]`.
- **url** (string (uri), required): Fully-qualified URL. Example: `"https://www.city-sightseeing.com"`.
- **headers** (HttpHeaders, optional): Headers object.
- **retryOnError** (boolean, optional): Whether retry on error is enabled. Example: `true`.

### `NotificationSubscriptionList`

Array of [`NotificationSubscription`](#notificationsubscription) — a list response, no fields of its own.

### `NotificationSubscriptionRequest`

- **notificationTypes** (string[], optional): List of notification type values. Example: `["STANDARD"]`.
- **url** (string (uri), optional): Fully-qualified URL. Example: `"https://www.city-sightseeing.com"`.
- **headers** (HttpHeaders, optional): Headers object.
- **retryOnError** (boolean, optional): Whether retry on error is enabled. Example: `true`.

## Integration notes

From [docs.ventrata.com/capabilities/notifications](https://docs.ventrata.com/capabilities/notifications).
All paths are under `/octo`.

### The three notification types

| Type | Fires when | `data` fields you receive |
|---|---|---|
| `BOOKING_UPDATE` | a booking changes | `uuid` |
| `AVAILABILITY_UPDATE` | availability changes | `productId`, `optionId`, `availabilityIds` |
| `PRODUCT_UPDATE` | a product changes | `productId` |

**`notificationTypes` is case-insensitive on the way in and uppercase on the way out.** Send
`booking_update` if you like; expect `BOOKING_UPDATE` back. Compare case-insensitively or normalise
before matching.

### The payload carries identifiers, not state

Every `data` payload is a set of IDs — never the changed object. So a notification is an instruction
to re-read, not a source of truth:

- **BOOKING_UPDATE** → `GET /bookings/{uuid}` with the `uuid` from `data`.
- **AVAILABILITY_UPDATE** → `POST /availability` for the `productId` / `optionId`, restricted to the
  `availabilityIds` listed. This is the one type that hands you an array: expect several slots per
  notification and batch the re-read.
- **PRODUCT_UPDATE** → `GET /products/{productId}`.

Treat the payload as untrusted: verify by fetching. A cache invalidated from the IDs and refilled
from the API stays correct even when a delivery is duplicated or arrives out of order.

### Subscribing

`POST /notifications/subscriptions` with a `url` and the `notificationTypes` you want. Two fields
decide operational behaviour:

- **headers** — an arbitrary header map sent with every delivery. The documented example is
  `{"X-Webhook-Secret": "whsec_123456abcdef"}`, which is how you authenticate an incoming call:
  the API has no signature scheme of its own, so this shared secret is the mechanism.
- **retryOnError** — when `true`, failed deliveries are retried. Leave it on and make your endpoint
  idempotent rather than relying on exactly-once delivery.

`subscriptionId` and `url` are required on the stored `NotificationSubscription`; on the request only
what you are setting. `GET /notifications/subscriptions` returns a **paginated** array.

### Notifications or webhooks

`octo/notifications` and `octo/webhooks` overlap. Notifications cover three types through
`/notifications/subscriptions`; webhooks cover four events — including `order_update` — through
`/webhooks`. Pick one per integration and stay with it: subscribing to both delivers the same change
twice. See [WEBHOOKS.md](WEBHOOKS.md).
